title: The bridge is the worst seat for the bats
why: Cold, problem-aware Austin visitors who plan to watch the bats from Congress Ave Bridge; flips them to the water before the colony leaves in early November.
hook_options: The bridge is the worst seat for the bats
1.5 million bats. You're watching the back of a stranger's head.
Everyone watches the bats from the bridge. That's the problem.
caption: Congress Avenue fills up every dusk. You get a railing, elbows, and the bats flying out under your feet. From a kayak they come out right over your head. A few weeks of bat season left before the colony heads south. #austinbats #congressavenuebridge #ladybirdlake #austinkayaktours

slides.headline: The bridge is the worst seat for the bats
slides.body: Hundreds of people, one railing, everyone craning sideways. There's a better seat. It floats.

slides.headline: You mostly see the people in front of you
slides.body: Congress Avenue packs up at dusk. Get there early for a railing spot, then watch the colony fly out under your feet.

slides.headline: The colony comes out over your head
slides.body: You sit on Lady Bird Lake beside the bridge and look straight up. No railing. No elbows.

slides.headline: A ribbon of bats that runs for minutes
slides.body: Up to 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats live under Congress Avenue Bridge. The biggest urban colony in North America.

slides.kicker: The fear nobody says out loud
slides.headline: Won't they fly into us?
slides.body: They're out hunting insects, not kayakers. One guest called their guide "really funny and reassuring" about how harmless the bats are.

slides.headline: "I was a little frightened at first"
slides.body: "...but after seeing all the bats circling up above and flying around, it was absolutely marvelous!" TripAdvisor review

slides.headline: The colony is starting to leave
slides.body: Fall cold fronts push the bats south. By early November most are gone until spring. Flights can run smaller and later now.

slides.headline: Nobody can promise a flight
slides.body: Bats are wild. Weather and temperature move the show. The sunset shows up every night, and that view alone earns the paddle.

slides.headline: Skip the railing. Sit under the colony.
slides.body: Guided sunset bat tours launch from 200 E Riverside Dr. About 2 hours. Kayak, paddle and life vest included.

slides.kicker: Save this for your Austin trip
slides.headline: A few weeks of bat season left
slides.body: Send this to whoever is planning the trip. Book the sunset bat tour at austinkayaktours.com.
